utterances.speaker: HALIT BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Revenge, what I understand by this term is the following. For the Serb that was killed in the shop, they killed 11 others, on the same day.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And -- and so that is the revenge. And for the other killings that occurred, was that also revenge? Is that -- is that what you are saying?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if it's revenge, but we know who gave the orders to commit all these crimes against the innocent civilians. This must have been given by those who issue orders, and that follows a certain hierarchy, institutions for all the killings that were committed in my municipality, especially for the killings of members of Berisha family.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I think the Court will be making determinations about -- I'm not going further into that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I was under an impression that this witness wasn't called here to testify as regards all the killings that happened in his municipality; therefore, he cannot be asked these questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, the answers have not advanced the Prosecution's case, so you needn't be concerned about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I think we just need to clarify one last point, and we'll need an exhibit for that. Could we see Exhibit 615, page 52, please, it's the map of Suva Reka that we've seen earlier. I would need the assistance of the usher, please, for just marking this. Now, can we turn this one time clockwise and zoom in maybe two clicks. I think that's fine. Let's leave it there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Berisha, you mentioned -- you asked about what direction the 20 to 30 members of the Berisha and Ramada Berisha families came from when you saw them at your house. Could I ask you to mark on this map where the families you mentioned lived?

utterances.speaker: HALIT BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the wine cellar here, and below this cellar, this is the area where they lived, the apartments where they lived. There is a long building here, and there is a passage that takes you to the main road. So they passed through this passage, went to the main road, and this is then a small lane that leads that area to my courtyard. So they came to my courtyard and then to the river. This is the march -- the route they made to arrive there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: HALIT BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this road here and the road that leads to Rastane is the road where the massacre was committed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: This might be difficult to understand later on. Let's --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Could you just make a circle just broadly around the area where they lived and I think that will do for the purpose that we need it.

utterances.speaker: HALIT BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Could we make that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is it --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The road to Rastane we've just --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I believe it's marked on the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But which road is it? Is it the road with the dotted lines on it, the grey road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The -- may I mark it?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Yeah --

utterances.speaker: HALIT BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the Rastane road.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That is the brown colour, the thinner of the two brown-coloured roads just near the junction of the two roads. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you --

utterances.speaker: HALIT BERISHA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the road to Rastane and the main road is here with red.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: It's marked at the end of that road. It cannot be seen, we haven't zoomed in enough, but it should be indicated there with a distance to the location.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Berisha.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I have no further questions for this witness, Your Honour. Oh, but I would -- sorry. I would ask that this image be made an exhibit, if you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just a moment, though, what is it you're saying can't be seen on it, the location of the massacre of the Berisha family?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: The -- no. The circle on this map indicates the area where the 20 to 30 members of the Berisha and Ramadan Berisha families lived.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I followed that. What is it you say cannot be seen on the map?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Well, there are a number of additional lines and dots and they may be without further markings difficult to understand. I think the witness indicated what route --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But you've just said: It's marked at the end of the road. It cannot be seen, but we haven't zoomed in enough but it should be indicated there with a distance to the location. What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: That is -- at the road you described there's marked on the map -- it's written -- well, I cannot see it we haven't zoomed in enough, 18 or 20 kilometres to Rastani.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I understand now. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did we get an exhibit number for this?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be IC41, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, were you going to say something?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just one clarification. It seems now that there is 18 to 20 kilometres to Rastani and I established with the witness that it's actually a suburb of Suva Reka and it's not on the map. We cannot see either 20 or 18 on this map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Berisha, are you -- you heard that comment. How far was it from where you lived to Rastani?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the road from Suhareke to Rastane is 3 kilometres and something, up to 3 and a half kilometres I would say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Well, that completes your evidence. Thank you for coming to the Tribunal to give it, and you're now free to leave.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honours, Ms. Carter will take the next witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is -- is there only one witness present?

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. And the witness will be?

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: The witness will be Ali Gjogaj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: And pursuant to the conversations that were being held with Defence earlier, the translation that had been requested by Mr. Ackerman, Ms. Grogan was kind enough to run those down and apparently the translation has been made. We actually have hard copies ready for the Defence teams in order to assist them in any sort of cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Gjogaj.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Would you please make the solemn declaration to tell the truth by reading aloud the document which will now be placed before you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated. Mr. Gjogaj, we know that you have been to this Tribunal before and that you gave evidence in the trial of Slobodan Milosevic. We have a copy of your evidence in that case. We also have copies of two statements that you've given to the Office of the Prosecutor. So we know a lot of material that you are able to give evidence about. The reason for you being here today is so that counsel for the Prosecution and for the various accused can ask you questions to either add to the material we already have, to clarify things in it, or to challenge it. The important thing for you is to concentrate on the question that each persons asks you and try to restrict your answer to the point that the question relates to. There's no point in repeating the things you've said before, unless you have to, to make the matter clear. We already have that. What we want is new or additional information. We want to know as much as we can and we want to try to avoid going over the things that we already know. So please concentrate on the particular questions that are asked. The first person to ask questions of you will be for the Prosecution, Ms. Carter. Ms. Carter.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. This witness is being submitted before the Tribunal as a 92 bis (D) witness. His name is Ali Gjogaj. We're requesting that his 92 bis package be accepted by the Court. It is transcript with the e-court number of P --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Let's -- we'll -- we don't need these details. Just let's get on with the evidence and you'll give us the exhibit number, no doubt, when we come to that little part of his evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Mr. Gjogaj, when you came to the Tribunal yesterday for proofing, did you have an opportunity to review all three statements that you have given before the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: And that review was done by having an interpreter read you out all three statements at your request. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Were the statements that were read out to you true and accurate copies of the statements that you have given before the ICTY?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Should I have three statements?

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. As part of the 92 bis package there are the two statements that we've been discussing quite extensively. There's a third statement with an ERN, it's a single page, of K0226430, the content is a single paragraph that's an addition to the first statement that was taken on February 27th of 2000. And, Your Honour, as these --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: As this is a 92 bis witness, we are asking for that 92 bis package under P2317 be tendered as well as the transcript under 2318, which includes also e-court number P00120, which are photos of an artillery range that were submitted during the Milosevic case on page 7390, line 21.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And are they legible?

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: The photographs?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Sir, I would like to actually speak with you a bit about the second statement that you had given that particularly relates to the exhumation of a firing range. When you initially gave statements before the Tribunal, you gave the first statement with regards to Pusto Selo. You later gave a second statement with regards to that firing range, but I want to set out a chronology. In regards to those events, which occurred first, the excavation of the firing range or the excavation -- excuse me, the Pusto Selo bodies?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ
utterances.text: The one at the firing range was the first.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: So that we can get an estimation in time, you indicated in that statement a broad range when you believe that exhumation actually took place. If we use the NATO bombings as a starting point, how long after the NATO bombings had begun did you excavate that firing range?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ
utterances.text: Since I don't remember dates, I am not good with dates, I know that it was in a week or two that we were told to exhume these bodies from the firing range.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: I want to discuss with you about the nature of that -- the job that you were asked to do. You indicated that you worked for a company called Hygijena. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: During your normal work day, what are the work hours that you are on shift at that company?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ
utterances.text: An eight-hour shift usually.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Is that eight-hour shift during what we would term a normal business day, starting between 8.00 or 9.00 and going until 5.00 or 6.00?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: When you worked for that company prior to the day that you were asked to excavate this firing range, had you ever been called into work in the middle of the night before?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ
utterances.text: On that day when we went to excavate the bodies, we were at work but at around 8.00 or 9.00 my boss came together with two colleagues of mine. He picked up -- us up in a Volkswagen Golf --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Please remember what I said to you. Answer the question you've been asked. Don't go over these matters. You were asked a very specific question. Before you were asked to do this job, had you ever been called in to work in the middle of the night?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. They collected us at around 8.00 in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Also with this company, was there any sort of night shift or any workers that ever did work overnight?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: So when your boss came to your home and brought you out to do this exhumation, that would be an extraordinary day. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ
utterances.text: Yes, it was an extraordinary schedule.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: When your boss arrived at your home, can you describe for me how he was dressed?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ
utterances.text: My boss had the clothes of the Yugoslav army.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Okay. When did your boss start wearing the clothes of the Yugoslav army?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ
utterances.text: He started wearing these clothes after the Serbs mobilised him.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: When was the mobilisation of the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ
utterances.text: As I said, I'm not good with dates, but simply when the Serbian army began to mobilise, that's when he put on his army clothes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Now I'm going to move through your statement actually to what is going to be the English page 3 as well as the B/C/S page 3. In it you describe a man on a small excavator as a man dressed in a green camouflage uniform. Is that a similar or the same uniform that your boss showed up at your house in?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ
utterances.text: The uniform was the same.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Outside of your boss and this man who was on the small excavator, were there any other men in a green camouflage uniform?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: You've indicated throughout the statement that there were men in blue camouflage uniforms that you identify as police. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ
utterances.text: Can you please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: You've indicated throughout your statement in regards to this firing range that at the firing range you saw a number of men in blue camouflage uniforms that you identify as police. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Did you see any police or anybody that you identify as police at that firing range?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ
utterances.text: When we went at the firing range, the -- everything had already been arranged. The police was there to protect us, and we started our work. And before went there, the work had not been started yet.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: When you said that the police were there, what were the police wearing?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ
utterances.text: It was the regular police.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: What do you mean by "regular police"?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ
utterances.text: It was kind of chequed -- I don't know how I've stated it in the statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Was it a solid uniform or did it have a pattern on it?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ
utterances.text: A solid uniform with a pattern.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: What colour was that uniform?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ
utterances.text: Green, the one that I have underlined.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Sir, are you referring to the pictures that were provided to you in the context of your first statement that are the camouflage patterns that were shown to you that was a NATO template. Is that what you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ
utterances.text: Yes. [Prosecution counsel confer].

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Your Honour, as of yesterday we were actually able to locate a copy, a coloured copy, of this camouflage pattern that is used on the back of several statements and we'd ask to use that colour copy on the ELMO in order to have the witness be able to identify what he's seeing.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour, objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We've never seen this and we want to know how many were offered on this colour pattern.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Your Honour, there's a black and white copy of it attached to the first statement of this witness. It's fairly clear it's four, which the Defence does have a copy of it, it just doesn't happen to be in colour. It's in black and white.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We've been asking for a colour one for a long time, and actually we've never seen it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, could I see it, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour. Your Honour, we just received this ourselves. There has been -- because of the request of the Defence as well as for our own use with our statements, we've been in contact with the Kosovo field offices. We have been talking to other investigators. We have been trying to find a colour copy of this. It came into our possession yesterday, and at that point in time it was used with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How come then we were --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, I would like to see it, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: And respectfully, Your Honour, this has been submitted to ERN'ing in order to provide a colour copy. It's in the process as opposed to something we can electronically disclose at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Show it to Mr. Lukic, please. This sort of thing can be avoided by informal indication of the fact that there's going to be an additional item and the exhibition of it to the Defence before we get into court.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Respectfully, Your Honour, it was the intention of the Prosecutor not to use this exhibit until there was an ERN'ing process. Only once the witness began referring to it and is clearly confused by the testimony he is giving at this point did I want to -- did I present it before the Court. It was not an intention to be used as a surprise. It was specifically going to be ERN'ed and then disclosed before we used it with any witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But it's an item that's arisen before and it was inevitably going to have to be in the a process in the case and therefore immediately when you had it you should have disclosed it.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we sent it for MIF'ing, it is in the process of being ERN'ing, it's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Look, don't talk to me in United Nations jargon. What does the world know about the ERN'ing process? Probably even less than I do. Let's talk in real language, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: What the Prosecution did once it received this document is that it sent it to the evidence section in order to have a number accounted for so that there could -- so that it could be released electronically, which has been the procedure we've used most of the exhibits with the Defence and we are still waiting for that process to be completed, where a number will be assigned to it. Once that number gets assigned, it comes back to us as a file through an e-mail. At that point in time it was going to be disclosed to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What do you have to say now that you've seen it?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: First of all, we would object because as we have seen before, the other witness showed at least 11 or 12 patterns he saw in his own village, so we think that it would be fair to show to the witness at least that much patterns, not to choose one out of two or out of four.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Your Honour, this -- this particular --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: If I want you to address me, I will invite you to address me.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic, please finish what you have to say. 3

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And we would object to this kind of pattern parade or recognition of patterns, where we have only four patterns offered. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It's so unfortunate that yet more time is wasted because something is produced in an inappropriate manner in court. It's very distressing that the routine conduct of this trial is constantly disrupted by these failures on the part of the Prosecution. Eventually it is going to be necessary for action to be taken, to try to bring home the importance of intimation of material at the earliest possible date. Having said these various things, it is plain to us that there will be no prejudice to the Defence by the use of this document. And therefore, we will permit its use. We consider it to be an adequate basis on which to test the witness's identification of uniform.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Thank you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So it can be put on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. And for clarification also of the record, I direct the Court to the witness's statement of February 27th of year 2000. The specific page number of K0075546 is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Ms. Carter, I have it in front of me. I know exactly what material you have here. Now we can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Sir, can you please indicate if you see a pattern or a colour pattern that looks like what you saw the MUP police wearing?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ
utterances.text: This one, this colour is the police colour.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Let the record reflect that it's the top left that was indicated of being the MUP police pattern.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, we have had an answer, have we, that they were MUP police?

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Yeah, he indicated police. I'm adding the MUP police. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Let's proceed on what the evidence actually amounts to.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The witness said "green uniform."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Indeed, but now we know what he thinks green is. That's a matter for cross-examination and testing in due course.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Sir, when you arrived at the firing range excavation site, you indicated that you saw police there and that you believed that they were protecting you. At some later point, did you see police doing additional tasks at the firing range?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: You indicate in your statement that there were two holes being dug at the firing range. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: You and the other employees of your company were in one hole. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Respectfully, Your Honour, I will not be using the ELMO any longer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That document will require a number at some stage.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, and we're seeking that document to be given the next IC number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be IC42, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Who was excavating the second hole at the firing range?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ
utterances.text: We were working at one of the holes, the people from the Hygijena company. The other hole was being done -- was being dug by the police.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: You indicate that there were refrigerator trucks on site. Were each of the holes being put into the same truck or different trucks?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ
utterances.text: No. In one of the holes where we were working we had one refrigerator truck, while the police had another.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: What was in the holes that you were excavating?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ
utterances.text: Corpses.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: In the excavation that you were doing, can you please describe for the Court how that took place. Was there -- was it being manually done or was machinery being used?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Why can't we just accept what's in the statement for this?

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Your Honour, there is an additional portion of it in regards to the machinery that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can you not get to that?

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Okay. Certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Sir, at some point in time, as opposed to having manual lifting of the bodies out of the hole, was there a point in time where the excavator, the machinery itself, was being used to lift corpses out of this exhumation site?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ
utterances.text: The bodies could not be taken out of the hole by hand; it had to be with an excavator because it was a very deep hole.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: And, sir, at the point in time where the excavator was being used to remove these bodies, was there ever an occurrence where dismemberment or other separation of the bodies was taking place?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ
utterances.text: Yes, of course that happened because the excavator could not take care of preserving the bodies. It was night as well, and the work was such that we were asked and everybody was required to bring these bodies out of the holes as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: And the bodies that were taken out of this mass -- would you -- was the hole itself, was it individual graves or was it a mass grave?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ
utterances.text: It was a mass grave.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: And in this mass grave, was it men only, men and women, men, women, and children? Who was in the hole that you were excavating?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ
utterances.text: They were civilians, all of them. They had civilian clothes on. It was night-time. I could not recognise the people, you know, the bodies, but the light of the excavator enabled us to see a little bit. And the light of the excavator helped us as well in that -- that we took the bodies from there and we put them in the refrigerator truck. And there were men, women, and children, all of them in civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Thank you. And, sir, after you finished clearing the hole that you were working on and the police cleared the hole they were working on, did you go to a second location?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: When you arrived at the second location, did you do a similar exhumation of a mass grave?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Okay. You indicated that you began these exhumations sometime in the night, well after your shift. What time did you complete the exhumation of the second site?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ
utterances.text: Well, I could respond about the first and the second site. Both of them finished at about 4.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: And given that the time was 4.00 a.m., is it fair to say that both of these exhumations took place in the cover of night?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is -- Ms. Carter -- well, sorry, I should ask the witness. You said that there were 80 to 90 bodies removed. Was that from one hole only?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One hole only, the first one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And is that one where you were working?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, the four workers of the Hygijena company, we exhumed about 80 or 90 bodies. I couldn't count them one by one, but the truck was full --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The second one you spoke of, who actually was removing the bodies from that hole?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The same workers, us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So what was it that the police were doing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When we were working at the firing range, we were working at the first hole and the police at the second one, while on the second site the police did not do anything with the holes. They just showed us where the bodies were, and we started working.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I was unclear that we were talking about one site with two holes and then another site. So going back to the first site where you said there were 80 or 90 bodies, did they come from only one hole, one grave?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One hole, where I was working, where we were working. I mean the Hygijena workers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And what was happening in the other hole where the police were digging?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, there might have been bodies there as well, but we were told not to interfere with their work. We continued with our work and they did their work. We didn't know what was happening.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Well, we'll break now and resume at five minutes past 6.00. Just leave the courtroom, Mr. Berisha -- Mr. Gjogaj. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Ms. Carter.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: One last topic for clarification. Sir, you indicated that this firing range was on the main road between Prizren and Suva Reka. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: And you've also indicated that you believe that this is a military firing range. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: How far away between Prizren and Suva Reka approximately was this range?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ
utterances.text: Approximately from Prizren at Lubishte was the police station. It was below this police station on the left side of the road going to Suhareke.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: And, sir, was this the only military firing range on the road between Prizren and Suva Reka?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ
utterances.text: Maybe there was at another location as well a firing range like that, but as for this one I know it was a military firing range.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: But, sir, I'm just talking about the brief distance between Prizren and Suva Reka. This is the only firing range. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. At this time I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. O'Sullivan.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: We will follow the order of the indictment, and I have no questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Fila.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't have any questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Visnjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No questions, Your Honour, but the way I understood was that this witness was to be cross-examined tomorrow. Perhaps I am not the right person to be saying this, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah, the only change was that the translation was delivered, but it was very recently. So have you -- are you likely to have questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Now, Mr. Aleksic, you may be one who does. Do you?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And is it Mr. Ackerman's intention to deal with this?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes, Your Honour, precisely so. This is what I was told by my lead counsel. I have read this document in Serbian, but without my lead counsel's consent we are unable to go on with the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I may have a few short questions, but I understood that I may begin my cross-examination tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You may if you wish. I just want to know if you wish to do it today.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe it would be better for me to go after Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. And, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I would like to use our right to start tomorrow, if possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Well, we've hit the buffers again, and we'll adjourn until tomorrow. Mr. Gjogaj, it's going to be necessary for you to return to complete your evidence tomorrow morning. The -- there may be questions from various counsel for the accused, and they understood that it would be tomorrow when these questions would be asked. That is an appropriate course to follow, so we will adjourn now. The important thing I have to say to you is that between now and tomorrow morning, when you return, you must not discuss your evidence with anyone, that means either the evidence you've given already or the evidence that you may give tomorrow. You can talk to anybody about anything else, but please do not discuss the evidence. All right? And we will see you back here again at 9.00 tomorrow morning. You may now leave the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We'll adjourn until 9.00 tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
